item.title: Innovation Lightbulb: FY 2027 Proposed R&D Cuts
item.description: The FY 2027 budget proposes deep cuts to federal R&D, threatening U.S. technological, economic, and national security leadership. As China expands state-backed research investments, reducing support for basic and use-inspired science risks weakening America's innovation edge.

item.title: Who Should Shape the Future of Development, and How?
item.description: As aid budgets shrink and the development landscape evolves, this commentary outlines key recommendations for civil society, philanthropy, and the private sector to rebalance power dynamics and build a more equitable development ecosystem.

item.title: Accelerating the EV Transition in the Global South Through India-Africa Partnership
item.description: India’s decade-long EV policy journey offers African nations a practical playbook. This white paper examines how South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria, and Egypt can accelerate electric vehicle adoption through India-Africa partnerships on manufacturing, minerals, and financing.

item.title: The Cyber Threat to the 2026 World Cup
item.description: The 2026 World Cup is an attractive target for malicious cyber actors, and even more so against the backdrop of ongoing geopolitical conflict. While preparation for such events is well rehearsed, maintaining resilience against threats will be paramount.

item.title: Solid Rocket Motors for Missile Defense: Challenges and Opportunities for Expanding the Industrial Base
item.description: Air and missile defense interceptors play a critical role in modern conflict. Accelerating production of solid rocket motors and strengthening the munitions industrial base will require an understanding of the market and both the challenges and opportunities for expansion.

item.title: Eurasia’s Shifting Balance of Influence: An Opening for the United States?
item.description: Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine and the ongoing conflict in Iran have created greater space for Washington to engage with Eurasia. Yet these developments have also provided more opportunities for other actors, including China, to expand their footprint in the region.

item.title: Who Are G7’s Top Performers?
item.description: The G7’s agenda has globalized even as the bloc’s share of the world economy and population has shrunk. As leaders convene at Évian-les-Bains, is the group still fit for purpose — and which countries actually perform on the issues it prioritizes?

item.title: Iran's Food Crisis
item.description: The war has exacerbated Iran's economic collapse and its cost-of-living crisis.

item.title: Trump's Iran Deal: What Comes Next? | State of Play
item.description: CSIS Middle East Program experts unpack the latest U.S.-Iran deal.

item.title: The New Carbon Order: China’s Response to Europe’s CBAM
item.description: China has been quietly building the institutional architecture needed to navigate the EU's carbon tariff regime.

item.title: The Truce Between the U.S. and Iran Was the Easy Part
item.description: CSIS's Daniel Byman unpacks the latest on a deal between the U.S. and Iran in Foreign Policy.

item.title: Energy Considerations for EXIM Reauthorization
item.description: Rejuvenating EXIM will be crucial to U.S. competitiveness as export credit agencies play an increasingly important role in global energy finance.

item.title: The United States and Iran Announce a Deal to End the War | State of Play
item.description: The United States and Iran will claim victory, but both have lost in important ways. The framework deal kicks negotiations on harder issues down the road and leaves key questions unanswered.

item.title: Southbound Diplomacy: Assessing Taiwan’s “Integrated Diplomacy” on the 10th Anniversary of the New Southbound Policy
item.description: As the New Southbound Policy marks its tenth anniversary, Henrietta Levin and Daniel Castro Bonilla evaluate opportunities for Taiwan’s new “integrated diplomacy” strategy to strengthen engagement with partners in South and Southeast Asia.

item.title: Everyone Lost the War With Iran
item.description: Will Todman in Foreign Policy unpacks how months of fighting revealed that multiple countries can impose costs, but none can impose order.

item.title: The Department of Commerce Restricted Access to Anthropic’s Latest Models. What Comes Next?
item.description: On June 12, the Department of Commerce imposed export controls on Anthropic’s latest models, causing abrupt disruptions in service and raising questions about future U.S. government AI policies. Our experts discuss next steps and alternate pathways.

item.title: U.S.-Canada Border Security: Fireside Chat with Sec. Markwayne Mullin and Hon. Gary Anandasangaree
item.description: The CSIS Americas Program hosted DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin and Canadian Minister of Public Safety Hon. Gary Anandasangaree to discuss U.S.-Canada border security.

item.title: States Weekly: June 17, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers June 17, 2026.

item.title: The Customs Executive Order: Dealing with Downstream Consequences
item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch discusses the implications of the Trump administration's "Strengthening Customs Enforcement" executive order, highlighting the increased costs and compliance challenges it may create for importers.

item.title: Industrial Athleticism: Calibrating Defense Production to Address Evolving Threats
item.description: The greatest threat to U.S. defense systems is not our adversaries — it's their obsolescence. To calibrate production for evolving threats with scarce resources, the U.S. needs an agile industrial base able to shift between surge, scale, and sustain acquisition strategies.
